objective: Test a compute-only torch.compile route for the existing full Qwen3-VL protocol without changing prompts, schemas, images, weights, candidate state, human truth, or training approval.

candidate.failure_summary: CUDA Graph output used by the static KV-cache path was overwritten by a later invocation; torch.compile requested an explicit graph step boundary or an out-of-graph clone.
compiler_diagnostics: Qwen3-VL vision rotary position code caused a Tensor.item graph break.
The decoder reached the torch._dynamo recompile limit because static cache layers changed initialization state.
The final failure occurred during Triton autotuning on a CUDA Graph partition.

restoration.method: Restarted the unchanged original service through the existing managed start script after the failed candidate process released GPU1.

cold_restart_replay_observation.interpretation: The candidate never served either sample, so this difference is not a candidate regression. It is evidence that an unchanged BF16 greedy service is not guaranteed to reproduce a cold result bit-for-bit across process restarts. Future engine gates must therefore combine fixed semantic acceptance criteria with repeated cold runs instead of assuming one exact hash is sufficient.

do_not_retry: Compiling the complete Qwen3-VL forward method with reduce-overhead CUDA Graphs on this runtime.
Any speed shortcut that changes the production prompt, schema, image budget, or candidate/truth boundary.
preferred: Evaluate a decode-only engine path that explicitly supports static KV-cache mutation, using repeated cold semantic gates.
Retain exact response reuse and adjacent-frame prefetch while engine work remains experimental.
Use the optional 5090 route only after existing external workloads naturally release enough memory.
